montessori.title: Montessori, in plain words
montessori.lead: What it looks like in our classrooms every day.

points.title: Children choose their work
points.body: Materials sit on low, open shelves. A child picks an activity, works with it for as long as they need, then puts it back for the next friend.

points.title: Hands first, then ideas
points.body: Counting rods, sandpaper letters and pouring jugs let children learn by touching and doing before they write anything down.

points.title: Teachers guide
points.body: Teachers prepare the room, show each material, then step back and watch for what each child is ready to learn next.

points.title: Small groups
points.body: Classes are kept small so each child gets individual attention.

programmes.title: Programmes by age
programmes.lead: PAC runs Montessori classes for children aged 2 to 6, plus childcare for families who need a full day. Each programme below has its own page.

nursery.name: Montessori Nursery
nursery.summary: A gentle first classroom with practical life, sensorial work, songs and stories.
nursery.intro: For 2 and 3 year olds, the first classroom is about feeling safe, doing things for themselves and getting used to a group. The Nursery is built around that.

sections.title: What children do
items: Practical life: pouring, spooning, buttoning, washing hands and tidying up, the everyday skills that build independence.
Sensorial work: sorting by colour, size, shape and texture to sharpen the senses.
Language: songs, rhymes and stories that grow vocabulary.
Music and movement, art and craft, and role play.

sections.title: How it runs
items: Small groups in our Taska building on Jalan Anggerik Aranda 31/34.
Session times: [SESSION TIMES TO CONFIRM]
Full-day childcare is available for working parents, from 6:30 am to 7 pm.

kindergarten.name: Montessori Kindergarten
kindergarten.summary: Phonics, hands-on maths and thematic projects, with preparation for Standard One.
kindergarten.intro: In the kindergarten years children start reading, writing and working with numbers. At PAC they get there with Montessori materials, a carefully graded phonics programme and topic-based projects, following the National Preschool Curriculum (KSPK).

sections.title: What children learn
items: Reading and writing through Montessori phonics: sandpaper letters and the moveable alphabet, then the Pink, Blue and Green reading series.
Mathematics with concrete materials, from number rods to the multiplication and division boards.
Thematic lessons and science that build responsibility and discipline.
Speech and drama for confident speaking.

sections.title: Getting ready for Standard One
items: Six year olds join the bridging class, which prepares them for Primary One.
The focus is reading, writing, speaking and problem solving in mathematics.
Lessons follow the National Preschool Curriculum (KSPK).

sections.title: How it runs
items: Tadika PAC, our kindergarten building, is at No. 1, Jalan Anggerik Aranda 31/170C.
Session times: [SESSION TIMES TO CONFIRM]
After-class childcare is available until 7 pm.

fullMontessori.name: Full Montessori class
fullMontessori.summary: One mixed-age class where younger children learn from older ones, as Montessori intended.
fullMontessori.intro: In a Full Montessori class, children from 2 to 6 share one prepared room. Younger children watch and copy the older ones; older children grow in patience and leadership by helping. Our founder calls this natural learning.

sections.title: Why mixed ages
items: Children move through the materials at their own pace, not their age group's.
Older children practise what they know by showing it to younger ones.
Care, cooperation and leadership grow out of daily life together.

sections.title: What's in the day
items: A long, uninterrupted Montessori work period.
Speech and drama, music and movement.
Science, cultural topics and outdoor play.

sections.title: How it runs

childcare.intro: Many PAC families have both parents working. Childcare wraps around the Montessori class, so your child can be dropped off early, stay through lunch and be collected after work.

about.title: A small Montessori school, run by the same founder since 1999
about.photo: The garden at Taska PAC, with tree-stump seats

story.title: How PAC started
paragraphs: Ms. Amy opened PAC's first Montessori-based taska in Kota Kemuning in 1999.
She chose small groups so that teachers could focus on each child. In 2007 a tadika followed in a second building on the same road, for children aged 5 and 6.
Today PAC runs age-grouped classes, a Full Montessori class where children aged 2 to 6 learn together, and full-day childcare for working families.

buildings.title: Two buildings, one school
buildings.body: Taska PAC houses the nursery, the Full Montessori class and childcare. Tadika PAC, a short walk along Jalan Anggerik Aranda, houses the kindergarten.

philosophy.title: What we believe about young children
philosophy.commitment: Our commitment: the development of the whole child.

points.title: Children build themselves
points.body: Through their senses and their own work, children construct who they are. Our job is to give them the right environment and the time to do it.

points.title: A prepared environment
points.body: Every room is calm, orderly and set up so children can reach, choose and put back their materials without help.

points.title: The teacher as guide
points.body: Montessori teachers are not there to command. They prepare the room, give short, careful lessons and observe each child closely.

points.title: Respect for work and for others
points.body: Children learn to respect their own work and their friends' work, and to find joy in finishing a task.

points.title: Behaviour as a message
points.body: When a child struggles, it usually means a need isn't being met. We observe first, then adjust.

points.title: Creativity and nature
points.body: Children are free to express themselves through art, music, story and play, and to spend time with living things.

about.materials: Our Montessori materials come from specialist suppliers in several countries, including India and the Netherlands.

curriculum.title: Six areas of learning
curriculum.lead: Montessori classrooms are organised into areas. Children move between them, choosing work from each, and teachers keep track of how every child is progressing.

areas.title: Practical life
areas.body: Everyday tasks that build independence, coordination and concentration.
examples: Pouring, washing and polishing
Tying and buttoning
Preparing snacks, like sandwich rolls and fruit salad
Putting work back where it belongs

areas.title: Sensorial
areas.body: Materials that train each sense, so children notice differences and put them into words.
examples: Grading by size, colour and shape
Matching sounds, smells and tastes
Feeling texture, temperature and weight
Recognising objects by touch alone

areas.title: Mathematics
areas.body: Number concepts built step by step with concrete materials, before moving to paper.
examples: Number rods
Sets, sorting and sequencing
The decimal system, for six year olds
Mixed sums, and the multiplication and division boards

areas.title: Language
areas.body: A carefully graded phonics programme. In Montessori, many children write before they read.
examples: Sandpaper letters and the moveable alphabet
Pink series: three-letter words
Blue series: blends
Green series: phonograms and digraphs, with early grammar

areas.title: Cultural studies
areas.body: Real objects and topic projects that connect children's surroundings to the wider world, including Malaysia's festivals.
examples: Botany and zoology: plants, animals and life cycles
Geography: globes, puzzle maps and maps of Malaysia
History: calendars, timelines and clocks
Science: the body, magnetism, push and pull, cooking

areas.title: Creative arts
areas.body: Self-expression where the process matters more than the result.
examples: Music and movement, rhythm and singing
Art and craft with water-based, non-toxic materials
Storytelling and role play
Speech and drama

projects.title: Science projects and outings
projects.body: Past projects have included hatching chicks, watching butterflies grow from caterpillars, and testing materials. Past outings have included Aquaria KLCC, Petrosains, a fire station and an ostrich farm in Semenyih.
projects.note: Outings are planned during the year. Parents are told in advance, and outing costs are paid by parents.

steps.title: Snack and outdoor play

steps.title: Thematic lesson and enrichment
steps.body: Group time for the current topic, songs and stories, or an extra class.

steps.body: Activities and play until parents arrive.

cycle.title: The work cycle, step by step

steps.title: Choose
steps.body: The child picks a material from the shelf, never from another child.

steps.title: Work
steps.body: They work with it for as long as they like, without being interrupted.

steps.title: Return
steps.body: They put it back, ready for the next child, then choose again.

cycle.note: Over the year, these cycles grow longer. That growing concentration is one of the clearest signs of progress.

rules.title: House rules at a glance
rules.note: This is a short summary. The full rules are given at registration.
items: Please give one month's notice before withdrawing your child.
Collect your child within 30 minutes of the dismissal time, or let us know if you'll be late. An overtime charge may apply.
Children aged 4 and above wear the PAC uniform.
Each child's temperature is checked on arrival. Children with a fever, flu or anything contagious should stay home.
Please keep your child's vaccinations up to date.
No jewellery, money, phones or toys from home.
No outside food except special diets.
Birthday cakes are welcome at snack time.

sections.title: Who we are
sections.body: Taska & Tadika PAC ("PAC", "we") runs a taska and a tadika at Jalan Anggerik Aranda, Kota Kemuning, 40460 Shah Alam, Selangor. This notice explains how we handle personal data under the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (PDPA).

sections.title: What we collect on this website
sections.body: When you book a visit, we collect your name, phone number, email address if you give it, your child's age range, your preferred date and time, your message and the language you'd like us to reply in. We don't ask for your child's name, MyKid number or medical details on this website, and we ask you not to include them.

sections.title: Why we collect it
sections.body: Only to reply to your enquiry and arrange a visit. We don't use it for marketing and we don't sell or share it.

sections.title: Who processes it for us
sections.body: Your request is sent to us by email using Resend, an email delivery service. A spam check by Cloudflare Turnstile may run when you submit the form. These providers process data on our behalf and may be located outside Malaysia.

sections.title: How long we keep it
sections.body: We keep enquiry emails for [RETENTION PERIOD TO CONFIRM] and then delete them, unless your child enrols, in which case the registration process applies.

sections.title: Cookies
sections.body: This website uses no advertising or analytics cookies. We remember your language choice in one small cookie. The map and the video tour only load, and Google or YouTube may only set cookies, after you click to show them.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You can ask to see, correct or delete the personal data we hold about you, or withdraw your consent, by emailing amypac2008@gmail.com or calling 016-272 9666.
